pinyin: bù míng zé yǐ, yī míng jīng rén
gloss: A quiet person surprises everyone when they finally speak.
teaser: Have you ever waited for the perfect moment to shine?
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Have you ever waited for the perfect moment to shine? [break 1s] The phrase is: 不鸣则已，一鸣惊人 (bù míng zé yǐ, yī míng jīng rén). [break 1s] 不 (bù) - not [break 0.5s] 鸣 (míng) - to chirp or make a sound [break 0.5s] 则 (zé) - then [break 0.5s] 已 (yǐ) - to cease [break 0.5s] 一 (yī) - one [break 0.5s] 鸣 (míng) - to chirp or make a sound [break 0.5s] 惊 (jīng) - to surprise [break 0.5s] 人 (rén) - person [break 1s] So, the idiom again: 不鸣则已，一鸣惊人 literally means "If one does not chirp, they will suddenly surprise people when they do." Figuratively, it suggests that a person who keeps quiet may astonish others with their talents when they finally express themselves. [break 1s] Here’s the story behind it: [break 1.5s] This idiom originates from a fable about a talented bird that remained silent for a long time. Once it finally sang, its beautiful voice amazed everyone around. This story emphasizes that sometimes, those who are quiet have much to offer, and when they finally share their gifts, it can be truly remarkable. [break 1.5s] Example 1: 他平时不说话，但考试时表现得非常好。 [break 1s] He usually doesn't speak, but performs exceptionally well during exams. [break 1s] Example 2: 她一直在为比赛练习，结果一上场就赢了。 [break 1s] She practiced for the competition quietly, and when she performed, she won immediately. [break 1s] Example 3: 这位作家多年没有发表作品，最近的新书让大家惊讶。 [break 1s] This author hadn't published anything for years, and their recent book surprised everyone. [break 1s] So, 不鸣则已，一鸣惊人 means a quiet person surprises everyone when they finally speak. Thank you for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom. [break 1s]
